chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from his uncle Muhammad from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, who said: Is'haq, the owner of the fish, narrated to me:

He said: We went out with fish to meet Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), and we had exited from Medina, and he (peace be upon him) had returned from a journey of his. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe be unto you, O so-and-so! Perhaps there is fish with you?' So I said: 'Yes, O my master, may I be sacrificed for you.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Descend, all of you!' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe be unto you, perhaps it is Siganus?' I said: 'Yes.' So I showed it to him (peace be upon him). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ride! There is no need for us with regards to it, and the Siganus is a fish which has no scales on it.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida, referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.زَهْو: Zahw, a specific type of fish mentioned in the narration
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحِيتَانِ: Sahib al-Hitan, meaning the owner or keeper of fish
key_terms.قِشْر: Qishr, meaning scales or skin, used here to denote the presence of scales on fish

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fish that do not have scales according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s precise knowledge of local marine biology, identifying 'Zahw' as a scaleless fish suitable for consumption despite lacking the typical 'qishr' (shell/skin) often associated with edibility in other traditions. The narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s infallible insight into both religious jurisprudence and natural sciences, serving as a foundational text for discussions on the criteria of halal seafood in Shia fiqh.
